To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the PISCF-allatostatin receptor has been identified and characterized in T. castaneu and the tissue distribution determined.
the PISCF-allatostatin receptor from the red flour beetle (Tribolium castaneun) has been cloned and characterized and its tissue distribution and expression pattern have been determined.

we have identified a novel allatostatin (AST) receptor in the red-flour beetle, Tribolum castaneum, that is activated by both AST and ASTCC, that has a broad tissue distribution, that is expressed in the brain and gut, and that is involved in the regulation the protease activity of the gut.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterisation of the Trica-PISCF/AST and the identification of the physiological role of this peptide in T. castaneurm.
the characterisation of a PISCF/allatoregulatory peptide receptor from a beetle and the biological activity of the PISCS/allatoregulatory peptides in beetles.
characterising the PISCF/allastostatin receptor from T. castaneu.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the PISCF-allatostatin receptor is a pleiotropic peptide that is involved in the regulation and biosynthesis of juvenile hormone, myoinhibitory in the gut and the ovary, and suppresses feeding in various insects but its roles in beetles is poorly understood.
the Trica-AST receptor and its cognate ligand, Trica-AST, are present in T. castaneun, and the Trica- AST receptor is activated by the insect PISCF-AST, Trica- ASTCC and Manse-AST.
the Trica-AST system has multiple roles in beetlemetamorphosis and development, and that Trica-ASTs may be myoinhibitory in some tissues, but not in others.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PISCF/allatoregulatory peptides and their receptors are present in the red flour beetles, but their physiological significance is not yet known.
the PISCF/allastatins (ASTs)/receptors are present in beetles and are likely to play a role in the control of feeding and/or reproduction.
Trica-AS is an important regulator of gut function in beetles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PISCF/allato-statin peptides are present in the red flour beetles and are likely to be involved in a variety of physiological processes.
Trica-AS has a widespread distribution in T. castaneun, suggesting it has multiple physiological roles.
the Trica-AST receptor has a widespread tissue distribution and may play a role in multiple biological processes in beetles.
